# `moonlight-service-volume`

Scenario kind of the engine v0.39.0, family [Lunar and cislunar](../lunar-and-cislunar.md). Advisory: analysis output from a research and engineering tool, not type-approved navigation equipment and not a safety-of-life service. Every label here is the engine's or the verification matrix's; a kind is MODELLED unless the matrix says otherwise (how a label is earned: the README's Evidence section).

## What it does

Modelled lunar navigation service-volume analysis from an ILLUSTRATIVE, public-source Moonlight/LCNS-class lunar-orbit constellation (not affiliated with ESA): sweeps a selenographic lat/lon grid over a time horizon and reports DOP / coverage / availability (≥4 sats AND PDOP < threshold) plus a generalised lunar ARAIM protection-level (HPL/VPL) envelope over the volume. The DOP geometry REUSES the gnss_lib_py-VALIDATED kernel (crate::orbit::dop); the protection level REUSES the LunaNet LNIS lunar ARAIM machinery (crate::lunar, σ_URE≈30 m) and reduces to the existing south-pole PL as a special case. MODELLED composition: a circular-/elliptical-Keplerian relay set (not the real differential-corrected LCNS/NRHO ephemeris), a mean-rotation Moon (no libration/precessing pole). Deterministic (pure geometry). No TRL/heritage/agency endorsement.

One run of `scenarios/moonlight-service-volume.toml` summarises as: moonlight-service-volume | 8 sats (illustrative LCNS-class, not affiliated) | 24 pts × 12 epochs | coverage 37.8% (PDOP<6.0) | sats 4–7 | PDOP 2.19/13.74/180.30 | HPL 139–4177 m | PL avail 0.0% | MODELLED

## Evidence

MODELLED: the [verification matrix](../../VERIFICATION-MATRIX.md) rows that name this kind.

- **MODELLED** The `lunar-surface` kind and phase: relay availability and PDOP, Earth and Sun visibility and a disciplined surface clock for each site and season, with the terrain skyline of `moonlight-service-volume`; a single-site run equals that kind's

The rows the run itself exercised, with the oracle the matrix gives each (the public sources are named there):

- **MODELLED** Deterministic, scenario-hashed, SBOM + cross-platform golden gates. Oracle (ExternalDataset): SBOM conformance to the official CycloneDX 1.5 JSON Schema (+ valid SPDX identifiers) — an external published standard, zero validation errors over the full dependency graph; the FoM-determinism / byte-reproducibility part remains a pinned self-consistency check, so the row stays MODELLED
- **VALIDATED** Moonlight-class lunar DOP / coverage / availability + generalised lunar ARAIM protection levels over a service volume. Oracle (ExternalDataset): Independent third-party authority ANISE 0.10.2 astro::Orbit Keplerian propagator (Nyx Space, MPL-2.0) — an equinoctial two-body code path distinct from kshana's Newton-Raphson Kepler; per-satellite MCI position agrees to <1e-3 m and the derived visible-satellite count/set matches exactly at every grid point. The DOP kernel is gnss_lib_py-validated; integrity uses published LunaNet/LCNS parameters
- **VALIDATED** Per-satellite topocentric look angles (azimuth clockwise from north, elevation) and slant range at a named selenographic site, given the satellite in the site's. Oracle (ExternalDataset): ANISE 0.10.2 (Nyx Space, MPL-2.0, run as a tool from xval/anise-service-geometry, binary lunar-look-angles-xval, which calls no Kshana code): ANISE's own azimuth, elevation and range routine (azimuth_elevation_range_sez) from sites built by its latitude-longitude-altitude constructor on the pck00011 Moon (sphere 1737.4 km), with the satellites rotated into MOON_PA_DE440 through moon_pa_de440_200625.bpc. 768 samples o
